title: Streaming + Backpressure-aware Retries for Embeddings & Rerank SDKs (Python/TS/Go) — ergonomic examples
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our embeddings and rerank endpoints support streaming token deltas and streaming rerank scores, but SDK ergonomics for streaming + retries diverge between Python/TS/Go. Engineers report awkward client-side patterns for resume-on-retry, inconsistent backpressure semantics, and missing canonical examples. This ticket implements a language-specific set of small shims and example guides: (1) backpressure-aware stream adapters that preserve order and allow transparent retry/reconnect, (2) a compact retry policy for partial stream failures that replays necessary context (prefix/KV pointers) rather than full request re-send, and (3) cross-language examples demonstrating idiomatic generator/async-iterator/chan usage for embedding + rerank streaming responses.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes a StreamingIterator with .resume(token_cursor) and built-in exponential backoff retry for transient stream interruptions; examples in SDK docs show generator-based usage and an async iterator variant.

TypeScript SDK exposes an AsyncIterable shim with explicit signal-based backpressure (AbortSignal + windowed queue) and a small helper `resumeFrom(cursor)` that integrates with existing pagination/batching helpers.

Go SDK offers a channel-based streaming adapter that supports context cancellation, reconnect with minimal re-sent payloads (cursor-based), and a sample demonstrating idiomatic usage in a web server handler.

All three SDKs include end-to-end examples for embeddings followed by rerank: batching N inputs, streaming embeddings, using embedding cursor to resume partial rerank requests, and a test harness that simulates transient network failure and verifies correctness (order preserved, no duplicate items beyond documented retries).
API parity checklist completed and reviewed by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) with one docs PR and one cross-SDK integration test in CI.
Performance: streaming adapters add <5% median latency overhead for steady-state streams; documented trade-offs in the design note.
Security: no plaintext token persistence in cursor state; security_review_required flagged if design stores any customer data in long-lived artifacts.
Follow-up tasks identified for console telemetry hooks (stream-level traces) and dedicated release notes for runtime-1.20.
discussion: 2026-02-25 Ava Martinez: Initial RFC sketched in Confluence (link below). Proposal favors small language-specific shims rather than a large cross-language abstraction to avoid ergonomic leaks.

2026-02-27 Rohit Desai: Prototype in Python demonstrates resume token and retry loop. Observed a race when consumer cancels while reconnect is in-flight; added an explicit lifecycle state machine to address it.

2026-03-02 Design review (Sofia Kim): Requested examples that show server-side usage for Go with context cancellation. Minor API wording suggestions for TypeScript helper names (suggest 'resumeFrom' vs 'resume').
2026-03-04 Engineering sync: Agreed on retry policy defaults: initial_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=5s, jitter=0.25, max_attempts=4. Documented in design note.

2026-03-06 QA update (Miguel Ortega): Added flaky test that simulates partial stream failure after 40% of items; found duplicate emission for one case — root cause: cursor advancement before ack. Patch in progress to ack after chunk processed.
2026-03-09 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/4127 adds StreamingIterator and tests. Reviewers: elena-ryan, tom-chen. CI currently failing on one flake.
2026-03-10 Rohit Desai: Merged TypeScript shim PR (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/2102). Working on Go adapter PR next. Scheduling docs PR for next week.

Notes: Keep retry behavior opt-out for customers who manage retries upstream. Provide clear examples for 'at-least-once' vs 'exactly-once' semantics (we document 'at-least-once with dedupe token' in examples).
notes: Trade-offs: we avoid persisting user payloads in resume cursors; cursors are opaque small blobs that reference server-side KV state. Chosen approach reduces bandwidth on retries but requires server support for cursor lifecycle. Implementation plan: land language shims -> docs -> cross-SDK integration test -> telemetry hooks. Follow-ups: add sample for controlled batching with prefix cache hints and add a migration guide for teams using existing streaming helpers.
